pr.title: Detect (non-raw) borrows of null ZST pointers in CheckNull
pr.description:
Fixes #136568. Ensures that we check that borrows of derefs are non-null in the `CheckNull` pass **even if** it's a ZST pointee.

I'm actually surprised that this is UB in Miri, but if it's certainly UB, then this PR modifies the null check to be stricter. I couldn't find anywhere in https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/behavior-considered-undefined.html that discusses this case specifically, but I didn't read it too closely, or perhaps it's just missing a bullet point.

On the contrary, if this is actually erroneous UB in Miri, then I'm happy to close this (and perhaps fix the null check in Miri to exclude ZSTs?)

On the double contrary, if this is still an "open question", I'm also happy to close this and wait for a decision to be made.

r? @saethlin cc @RalfJung (perhaps you feel strongly about this change)
pr.author: compiler-errors

issues.title: Null ptr check doesn't catch null reference to ZSTs
issues.body:
As https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/134424 recently landed, for the following code, I'd expect the check will catch null reference as Miri does, but actually not:

```rust
// Based on the description of PR#134424, but using a ptr to ZST
let ptr: *const () = std::ptr::null();
let _val: &() = unsafe { &*ptr };
```

As per https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/472 , access to a ptr to ZST is not UB, so  `*ptr` is ok.

```rust
$ cargo run
# **No panic** like "null pointer dereference occured"
```



But it could be better to catch null reference `&*ptr`:


```rust
$ cargo miri run
error: Undefined Behavior: constructing invalid value: encountered a null reference
 --> src/main.rs:3:30
  |
3 |     let _val: &() = unsafe { &*ptr };
  |                              ^^^^^ constructing invalid value: encountered a null reference
  |
  = help: this indicates a bug in the program: it performed an invalid operation, and caused Undefined Behavior
  = help: see https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/behavior-considered-undefined.html for further information
```

Not sure if I put up a real issue. I just thought the check would act on null reference, since in some cases [the term pointer may refer to a reference as well](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/types/pointer.html).

I guess we need another check for null reference, because null ptr is not harmful, dereferencing to it is harmful, while it doesn't need dereferencing for null reference to be UB.

analysis.summary: CheckNull previously guarded every null-pointer check with a "pointee is not a ZST" test, so a null raw pointer dereferenced in a borrow context (`&*ptr` or `&mut *ptr`) to a ZST was not checked. The fix makes borrow contexts check unconditionally, while reads and raw borrows of null ZST pointees remain allowed.
analysis.originalLogic: In `insert_null_check`, CheckNull computed `sizeof_pointee = SizeOf(pointee_ty)` and `is_pointee_no_zst = sizeof_pointee != 0`, then panicked only when `is_null & is_pointee_no_zst`. The original code comment stated: "Get size of the pointee (zero-sized reads and writes are allowed)." and "We want to throw an exception if the pointer is null and doesn't point to a ZST." Thus any null dereference whose pointee was zero-sized was skipped regardless of how the place was used.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation used the same ZST-size guard for all place-use contexts: `should_throw_exception = is_null AND (sizeof(pointee) != 0)`. For a null `*const ()` or other null ZST pointee, `sizeof(pointee) != 0` is false, so even `let _ptr: &() = unsafe { &*ptr };` produced no runtime check, even though constructing a reference from a null pointer is UB. The correct transformation replaces that guard with the constant `true` when `context` is `PlaceContext::NonMutatingUse(NonMutatingUseContext::SharedBorrow)` or `PlaceContext::MutatingUse(MutatingUseContext::Borrow)`, and keeps the non-ZST guard for all other contexts. The patch comments this invariant: "Borrows pointing to \"null\" are UB even if the pointee is a ZST." and "Other usages of null pointers only are UB if the pointee is not a ZST."
analysis.trigger: A MIR place read through a null raw pointer whose pointee type is zero-sized, where the place is consumed as a shared borrow (`&*ptr`) or mutable borrow (`&mut *ptr`) under `-C debug-assertions`. Plain reads of the same null ZST pointee (for example `let _ = *ptr;`) and raw borrows (`let _ = &raw const *ptr;`) are allowed and must not trigger the null check.
preconditions: CheckNull runs as part of the pointer-check MIR pass under `-C debug-assertions`.
The dereferenced pointer value is null at runtime.
The pointee type has size zero, so the old `SizeOf(pointee_ty) != 0` guard is false.
The place use context is a shared or mutable borrow, not a plain read or raw borrow.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR functions containing a dereference of a raw pointer, parameterized by (1) pointee size: ZST versus non-ZST, (2) place-use context: shared borrow, mutable borrow, plain read, raw borrow, and (3) pointer value: null versus non-null. This lets a test generator produce two programs differing only in the place-use context (for example `&*ptr` versus `let _ = *ptr`) or only in pointee type (`()` versus `u32`), while holding the null pointer construction fixed.
pitfalls: Do not make the null check unconditional for every context: zero-sized reads and raw borrows of null pointers are explicitly allowed, and an unconditional check would introduce false positives.

`&raw const *ptr` is not the same PlaceContext as `&*ptr`; raw borrows must remain guarded by the non-ZST test. The added `place_without_read_zst.rs` run-pass test and the `&raw const *ptr` line added to `place_without_read.rs` guard this distinction.
Mutable borrows use `MutatingUseContext::Borrow`, not the shared-borrow context, so both borrow variants must be handled.

CheckAlignment's `insert_alignment_check` receives the new `PlaceContext` parameter but names it `_context`; the context is only consumed by CheckNull, so alignment behavior should not be inferred to change from this patch.
The PR also fixes the diagnostic spelling from "occured" to "occurred"; UI test error patterns were updated, so an old error-pattern string can make a correct run appear to fail.
The issue notes that `*ptr` to a ZST is not itself UB, while constructing a reference `&*ptr` is UB; do not conflate the dereference place with the borrow of that place.
analysis.testStrategy: Use UI tests with `-C debug-assertions`. For the failing case, add `//@ run-fail` and `//@ error-pattern: null pointer dereference occurred` with a null ZST pointer borrowed as a reference, e.g. `let ptr: *const () = std::ptr::null(); let _ptr: &() = unsafe { &*ptr };`. For the negative cases, add `//@ run-pass` programs that read a null ZST (`let _ = *ptr;`) and take a raw borrow (`let _ = &raw const *ptr;`), ensuring no check is inserted for places that do not read. Pair ZST and non-ZST variants (as the patch does with `borrowed_null`/`borrowed_null_zst` and `place_without_read`/`place_without_read_zst`) so the only varying dimension is pointee size or place-use context. Update all expected diagnostic strings to "occurred".
evidence: Ensures that we check that borrows of derefs are non-null in the `CheckNull` pass **even if** it's a ZST pointee.
// Borrows pointing to "null" are UB even if the pointee is a ZST.
// Other usages of null pointers only are UB if the pointee is not a ZST.
// Get size of the pointee (zero-sized reads and writes are allowed).
// We want to throw an exception if the pointer is null and doesn't point to a ZST.
// We want to throw an exception if the pointer is null and the pointee is not unconditionally
// allowed (which for all non-borrow place uses, is when the pointee is ZST).
// Make sure that we don't insert a check for places that do not read.
error: Undefined Behavior: constructing invalid value: encountered a null reference
As per https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/472 , access to a ptr to ZST is not UB, so  `*ptr` is ok.
this PR modifies the null check to be stricter
